editorial.headline: Household Textiles: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A foreigner cannot register this specialist household-textile retail activity in Bali today, despite a nationally open foreign-ownership ceiling.
editorial.body:
A foreigner cannot register KBLI 47512 in Bali today. That is the practical starting point for a specialist retail activity that is nationally open to foreign ownership, yet falls within Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities.

The activity is the specialist retail sale of household textile goods: tablecloths, bed sheets, tarpaulins, pillowcases, mosquito nets, mattress and pillow fabrics, mops, household linen, and also pillows and bolsters. The emphasis is on the home-textile assortment itself, giving the classification a clear commercial identity around the materials and soft furnishings that shape domestic spaces.

It is available across the full business range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In national terms, then, the record presents no foreign-equity cap below full ownership. That national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, but it does not erase the regional condition recorded for Bali.

In Bali, the activity is marked BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, placing it inside the Bali moratorium that blocks all such KBLI activities from PMA registration. The restriction is island-wide and permanent; the record identifies the moratorium as taking effect in May 2026. For a foreign investor, the distinction is decisive: national openness describes the ownership ceiling, while Bali’s risk-based rule prevents PMA registration for this activity on the island.
